Case study · Private draft

Designing the future contact center with an AI-native process

How case management moved from Salesforce to Amazon Connect, and what changed when the whole design process started from shared context and coded prototypes instead of Figma.

ProjectCase management, internal tool for customer service agents
ShiftSalesforce to Amazon Connect
Pilot caseLost parcel
Primary goal20% lower average handling time

The problem

Agents switch between many tabs and tools to resolve one case. That is an internal pain, but it is really a consumer problem: longer hold times, repeated calls for the same order, and trust in the brand lost after the purchase moment.

Agents also spend around five minutes after each contact filling in details, and handoffs between agents are mostly manual.

Primary KPI

AHT, 20% reduction

Secondary KPIs

NPS and first contact resolution

Open question

Copy Salesforce processes, adopt Amazon Connect as is, or something in between?

The approach: context first

Instead of starting in Figma, the process started with a single space holding everything known about the project, so any new PO or designer, and the AI agent, work from the same memory.

Research reuse

Past agent surveys, Miro maps, VoC and a 360 Tracker of continuous agent feedback, mapped against each other.

Today vs tomorrow

Information architecture and heuristic evaluation of Salesforce and Amazon Connect side by side, including help for new agents.

Journey mapping

Tier 1 agent journey for the lost parcel pilot, tied to knowledge articles and to the pain point at each stage.

Card sorting

50+ agents across markets sorted info into must have upfront, useful, rarely needed, never needed, or missing.

Prototypes as code

The custom area in Amazon Connect is the middle panel, an iframe, so the prototypes focus there. They are coded and live in a GitHub repository, so the vendor sees the real tokens, spacing and flows instead of static frames.

Two directions were built quickly to drive stakeholder discussion: a custom vision and a native one using Amazon's own components. Scenarios included solved cases, auto-closed cases, waiting on customer, and a duplicate profile callout.

When there is something people can play with, it is much easier to get feedback than when business decisions are made without seeing what they look like.

Learnings

Craft matters more

Speed is not the point. The tool amplifies whoever drives it, like the move from Illustrator to Sketch to Figma.

Figma as sketch partner

Used for quick mockups so the AI understands intent, not for full pages.

Design systems must be LLM friendly

AI understood Amazon Connect's design system much better than the internal one.
